title: Buddy Petit's clean round tone and repertoire
summary: Punch praises Buddy Petit's round tone, soft playing and tunes like Maple Leaf Rag and High Society, with a break for stomach trouble.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: That's right. But he was strong, though. But the fella I only ever liked to play for me was Buddy Petit. I liked his play. I liked the way he played. Round, pretty. He didn't make high notes, but everything he made was clean.
Well, Buddy couldn't go enough for a G, you know.
No, how loud would he get?
He didn't play loud. I'll tell you the truth, he didn't play loud.
Did he feature slow tunes or fast tunes?
Do you remember any numbers he used to play? Do you remember any numbers that he used to play, any tunes?

Well, a couple of something like that. Bucket got a hole in there, it was just famous. Maple Leaf Rag, he used to play tough stuff, you know. Palermo Rag, Hard Society, he played all that. Now, I tell you what he did on Hard Society. He never played the lead this part. He never played that. He played the lead. He played the lead.
He played all the time. Let the clang out or something else take the lead.
He played on second all the time.
Would he let the clang out take the lead much on other tunes?

Yeah, no, not very. Yeah, but the other tune that he couldn't, thought he wasn't going to get up to, you know. No. Something like, uh, like when the thing come out and Palermo Rag and that run. Well, he'd play down and Zeb, the clang that played would play it up. He'd play it up. See, he'd play it up. He'd play it up. But Zeb, he'd play it up. See, and it sounds good too. Yeah. Sounds good. He never was a high note fella, but he could play a nice horn. Oh, what's the matter? Now, it's a tumble. Gas. All in there. Want to turn it off for a minute? Nothing but gas. It ain't about me. Just, I mean, I'm worried.
Well, you want to take some medicine, let us know.
I'll take medicine. Yeah, this morning man, I'll take no more medicine.
